name: Outsider House
about: Outsider house is the name a 2012 FACT article gave to the rough, hissy, noise-adjacent house coming out of Ron Morelli's L.I.E.S. label in New York, Opal Tapes in Britain and Vancouver's 1080p: tracks recorded to tape on cheap gear, with the kick drum distorted, the chords buried and the structure loose enough to feel improvised. Legowelt, Delroy Edwards, Huerco S., Ital, Madteo and Hieroglyphic Being were its touchstones, with Chicago's Jamal Moss and Detroit's Omar-S as the roots. The term was disowned by almost everyone it described, but it caught a real moment when noise musicians picked up drum machines, and it led directly to lo-fi house.

albums.title: Just Ask the Lonely
albums.why: The FXHE debut is the Detroit precedent for everything here: raw machine house, hiss intact, released without any concession to polish.

albums.title: Hazyville
albums.why: Darren Cunningham's debut dragged house through fog and tape distortion before the term existed; the London end of the outsider idea.

albums.title: LP
albums.why: Ren Schofield's first LP for Spectrum Spools is noise-scene techno at full distortion, and the record that set the template for the whole moment.

albums.title: The Paranormal Soul
albums.why: The Dutch veteran's Clone album is warm, lo-fi Chicago-style house on old hardware; proof that the outsider stance could also be tender.

albums.title: Hive Mind
albums.why: Daniel Martin-McCormick's Planet Mu debut chops Lady Gaga and Whitney Houston into loose, hissy house; the scene's manifesto record.

albums.title: Dream On
albums.why: Released the same year, Dream On is longer and more hypnotic, with the loops stretched past comfort; the better of the two to live with.

albums.title: Noi No
albums.why: Matteo Ruzzon's Sähkö album is the most alien record on this shelf, house reduced to murmurs, hiss and barely tethered drums.

albums.title: Music for Shut-Ins
albums.why: The L.I.E.S. compilation that defined the label and the term, with Delroy Edwards, Steve Summers and Svengalisghost at their rawest.

albums.title: Unicursal Hexagram
albums.why: Matthew Morandi's L.I.E.S. album is tape-saturated kosmische as much as house; one of the label's deepest early records.

albums.title: Spit
albums.why: The L.I.E.S. boss's own debut, on Dominick Fernow's Hospital Productions, is bleak, broken techno; the noise connection made explicit.

albums.title: Colonial Patterns
albums.why: Brian Leeds' Software debut buried house and ambient under layers of tape murk, and it became the scene's best-loved album.

albums.title: Needs Continuum
albums.why: Gwyer's No Pain in Pop album is improvised, long-form hardware techno with an ambient drift; outsider house's most exploratory record.

albums.title: Body Issues
albums.why: Max Ravitz's Opal Tapes release is the British label's signature: lo-fi hardware house that fades into ambient and back.

albums.title: Mimesiac
albums.why: A L.I.E.S. album of acid-tinged, drifting hardware techno, and one of the label's most carefully built records.

albums.title: American Noise
albums.why: The second L.I.E.S. compilation, two discs wide, catches the label at its peak and shows how far its rough house could stretch.

albums.title: Let's Cry and Do Pushups at the Same Time
albums.why: Luke Wyatt's Mexican Summer album is VHS-grade guitar, drum machine and tape haze; the outsider aesthetic as hazy Americana.

albums.title: Much Less Normal
albums.why: The 1080p release that put Vancouver on the map, with Ocean Dub; melodic, hissy house with a softer touch than New York's.

albums.title: Garifuna Variations
albums.why: Philippe Hallais built an album from Garifuna rhythms and broken hardware; outsider house as unresolved, deliberately awkward experiment.

albums.title: Hangin' at the Beach
albums.why: The L.A. Club Resource founder's thirty-track album is a sketchbook of lo-fi house, boogie and tape fragments; the scene at its most generous.

albums.title: The Disco's of Imhotep
albums.why: Jamal Moss's Technicolour album is his cosmic, Sun Ra-inspired Chicago house at its most focused, and the clearest entry to his vast catalogue.

albums.title: Plant Age
albums.why: Matt Gardner's L.I.E.S. album is dubbed-out, blurred house for headphones, and the late, meditative end of the outsider story.

note: Outsider house was a label and cassette culture, so this shelf leans on L.I.E.S., Opal Tapes and 1080p releases and stops at twenty-one.
